title: What sharing saves
description:
When several processes use the same DLL, Windows keeps **one** copy of its code in memory and maps it into all of them. Write two functions:

- `long long sharedSavings(long long codeBytes, int processes)`: how many bytes of memory sharing saves compared with every process having its own copy. With one process (or none) nothing is saved.
- `long long pagesFor(long long bytes)`: how many 4096-byte pages are needed to hold `bytes` bytes. A part page still takes a whole page; 0 bytes take 0 pages.

```
sharedSavings(1'000'000, 4) == 3'000'000      // four copies would cost 4 MB; sharing costs 1 MB
pagesFor(4097) == 2
```
hints: Sharing costs one copy instead of `processes` copies, so it saves `processes - 1` copies.
lessonTitle: What a DLL Is and Why Programs Use Them
